import html from typing import Dict # Define the invitation format template with placeholders. INVITATION_FORMAT: str = """

{event_title}

{event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def render_event_invitation( event_title: str, event_description: str, event_date: str, additional_notes: str ) -> str: """ Render a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- event_title : str The title of the event. event_description : str Full description of the event (may contain newlines or formatting). event_date : str The date of the event. additional_notes : str Any user‑provided notes about the event. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready for rendering in a web page. Notes ----- All user‑supplied content is escaped using `html.escape` to prevent XSS. The description and notes are wrapped in `
` tags to preserve line breaks
    while still escaping dangerous characters.
    """
    # Helper function to escape and wrap multiline content
    def _escape_and_pre(text: str) -> str:
        escaped = html.escape(text, quote=True)
        # Preserve line breaks by wrapping in 
        return f"
{escaped}
"

    # Prepare a mapping for string formatting
    context: Dict[str, str] = {
        "event_title": html.escape(event_title, quote=True),
        "event_date": html.escape(event_date, quote=True),
        "event_description": _escape_and_pre(event_description),
        "additional_notes": _escape_and_pre(additional_notes),
    }

    # Safely format the template
    sanitized_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format(**context)

    return sanitized_html.strip()
